title: Dynamic billing attribution matrix for marketplace commitments
creator: Avery Collins
description: Create a flexible, auditable attribution matrix that assigns invoice line items and commitment discounts across multi-tenant marketplace transactions and commitment splits. This ticket scopes the product rules, UI intake, and acceptance criteria for an initial MVP to reduce manual finance work and improve accuracy for enterprise customers who use marketplace credits and shared commitments.
background: Enterprise customers selling through the Redwood marketplace report frequent disputes during invoicing when usage spans multiple cost buckets (hosted API vs dedicated capacity) or when marketplace revenue needs to be split between partner and Redwood. Current process is manual: finance exports usage, runs spreadsheets, and issues post-invoice adjustments. This causes delays, support load, and undermines trust for large commitments.
problem_statement: We need a deterministic way to map usage to invoice allocations and to apply commitment or marketplace discounts consistently across billing periods, with an interface for finance and account teams to override or audit allocations.
goals: Reduce manual invoice adjustments for marketplace/commitment cases by 80% in first 6 months
Provide an auditable allocation graph for every invoice line (which rule produced allocation and which override was applied)
Ship an MVP that supports: (a) rule-based percentage allocation by product route, (b) partner revenue split, and (c) manual override and audit trail
non_goals: Full downstream accounting export format (QBO/NetSuite) for MVP
Automated tax calculation or global VAT rules
Complex time-weighted allocation across billing cycles in MVP
proposed_solution_summary: Add a billing attribution engine that evaluates ordered rules to assign usage tokens and costs to named buckets (customer invoice, partner split, commitment pool, marketplace fee). Expose a Console UI for finance/admins to define rule precedence and to preview allocations for a billing period. Persist decisions and overrides in an immutable audit log. Provide an API endpoint for engineering/finance automation to query allocation results for a billed period.
acceptance_criteria: Rules editor in Console that allows defining allocation by: route regex, model tag, deployment type (hosted|dedicated|private), and percent allocation
Preview mode that runs against a selected billing period and shows per-customer per-route allocations with estimated invoice lines
Immutable audit log entry for every allocation run plus metadata: rule-id, timestamp, actor (system|user override), and diff against previous run
API endpoint /billing/allocations?period=YYYY-MM returns JSON (MVP contract) with per-customer allocations matching Console preview
Manual override flow: finance can mark an allocation as 'finalized' for a billing period which prevents re-running unless unlocked
End-to-end tests validating allocation math for sampled scenarios including: split 70/30 partner, 100% commitment pool first, and route-based default fallback
implementation_tasks: Product: draft detailed rule DSL and Console wireframes (route matching, model tags, allocation percentages)
Design: build mockups for rules editor, preview table, and audit timeline
Engineering: billing service - add allocation engine module, persist allocation_runs table with rule refs
Engineering: Console - rules CRUD, preview runner UI, overrides UI, finalize/unlock actions
Engineering: API - implement /billing/allocations and appropriate pagination/caching
Analytics: add telemetry for allocation-run durations, preview hits, and number of manual overrides
Finance/Legal: define acceptable SLA and retention for audit logs and dispute window
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect allocations could cause revenue leakage or customer disputes. Mitigation: Preview-first workflow and required two-person signoff for finalizing allocations for enterprise invoices
Risk: Performance of running allocation preview on large datasets. Mitigation: sample-based preview for huge accounts and background batch jobs with caching for final runs
Risk: Rule complexity leading to confusing precedence. Mitigation: Provide default rule templates and visualization of precedence chain in UI
open_questions: Should commitment pools be exhausted in a deterministic order (oldest-first) or pro-rata across routes?
Do partners require separate tax handling that affects allocation percentages?
What is the minimum required retention window for audit logs for enterprise contracts (12/24/36 months)?
